body.p: AMENDMENTS TO THE CLAIMSThis listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application:

br.br:
1. (Previously Presented) A protective aircraft cover having a surface and at least one edge portion, said cover comprising:a material having a thickness; and
programmable magnets joined to said material for adhering said protective aircraft cover to an aircraft, said programmable magnets each comprising a single metal piece comprising a plurality of magnets joined together side-by-side with some of said magnets oriented with their North-South poles in one direction interspersed with other magnets oriented with their South-North poles in the opposite direction.
2. (Previously Presented) The protective aircraft cover according to Claim 1 configured to cover one of an engine inlet, and engine exhaust, and a Pitot tube.
3. (Previously Presented) The protective aircraft cover according to Claim 1 wherein said material is a collapsible material comprising a fabric.
4. (Previously Presented) The protective aircraft cover according to Claim 3 wherein said fabric is a fire resistant ballistic fabric including antistatic fibers.
5. (Previously Presented) The protective aircraft cover according to Claim 4 wherein the programmable magnets are encapsulated by stitching the fabric around said programmable magnets.
6. (Previously Presented) The protective aircraft cover according to Claim 5 wherein the collapsible material thickness is sufficient to prevent the magnetic field strength of the programmable magnets to cause adherence to one another.
7. (Previously Presented) The protective aircraft cover according to Claim 1 wherein at least one of said programmable magnets is programmed to have a magnetic field strength in a portion different from the magnetic field strength in other portions.
8. (Previously Presented) The protective aircraft cover according to Claim 1 wherein a combination of one or more material thickness and a magnetic field strength of said programmable magnets enables adherence to an aircraft surface subject to wind loads greater than 40 mph.
9. (Previously Presented) The protective aircraft cover according to Claim 1 wherein the programmable magnets have a magnetic field strength sufficient to adhere the protective cover to an aircraft while not causing damage to surface coatings.
10. (Previously Presented) The protective aircraft cover according to Claim 9 wherein the programmable magnets have a magnetic field that does not interfere with electronic signals when installed on an aircraft.
11. (New) The protective aircraft cover according to Claim 1 wherein some of the plurality of magnets comprising the single metal piece that comprises the programmable magnets have the same polarity and are joined directed to each other side-by-side.
